correctness.rationale: For the precisely defined p-curvature coefficient subscheme on split E×Y with E ordinary and Y elliptic, the restricted Jacobson identity gives T(f)=f^p+delta^(p-1)f-hf=0. Riemann–Roch on genus-one Y gives dim H^0(Y,O(D))=d, with residue map kernel constants and image the zero-sum hyperplane. For each F_p-valued residue vector, p-surjectivity of Pic^0(Y)(k) constructs a log-derivative f_j solving T=0. Writing f=c+sum b_j f_j, additive p-polynomial and independence of 1,f_j^p produce exact polynomial ideal (c^p-hc,b_j^p-b_j). Requiring every residue nonzero leaves N_p(d)=((p-1)^d+(p-1)(-1)^d)/p residue-indexed torsor summands, each length p. Ordinary Y has p geometric points per summand; supersingular Y has one nonreduced point per summand, even in p=2 and with no points if p=2,d odd. IMPORTANT TERMINOLOGY: residue-indexed summands are not necessarily connected components: for ordinary Y each Z/p summand is p separate connected points; the stated explicit scheme decomposition and geometric point count distinguish this. Independent exact finite enumeration reproduced residue formula for p=2,3,5,7 and small d; universal proof is scheme-theoretic, not derived from tests.
